title: I built a card game inside my AI companion game — keeping the rules separate from the conversation
author: Think-Shoulder-4960
selftext:
I'm the solo developer behind TyR Games, working on PEN 'n' DAITING. It combines AI companions, conversations and pen-and-paper adventures. One part of it is Roses & Runes: a collectible card game with four factions, 16-card decks and three locations.



The design choice I wanted to share is keeping the card rules in a separate resolver from the companion conversation. The dialogue gives the opponent personality, while the resolver handles legal moves and the actual game state. When I change the rules, I version them so an existing saved match keeps the rules it started with.



A separate lesson from generated characters: changing a default prompt doesn't necessarily change what an existing character sends. My app preserves saved templates, so old neutral hand-pose wording could survive an update. I now replace recognised, unchanged legacy defaults when constructing new prompts, while keeping custom wording and existing pictures. Checking the final prompt text caught this; checking only the new template wouldn't have.



Here's a short edited alpha clip of the card-game factions:

[https://www.youtube.com/shorts/6W1019tiCVA](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/6W1019tiCVA)



For people building games with persistent AI characters: how do you update defaults without unexpectedly changing a player's customised character? Do you version the whole character setup, individual prompt sections, or something else?



Disclosure: this is my commercial alpha project. It uses AI-generated artwork and dialogue, with AI assistance in development and marketing. The demo download is free, the full alpha is US$1.99, and live AI features require a provider account with separately paid credit.
